title: Experimental and theoretical investigations on the phase stability and mechanical properties of Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 high-entropy alloy

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Phase stability of the Cu-rich non-equiatomic Cr7Mn25Co9Ni23Cu36 HEA on annealing, and its effect on tensile properties, is unestablished. Annealing temperature and holding time should change which phases the alloy contains and therefore its tensile behaviour.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (DES/method), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: As-cast and after 2 h at 200-600 C the alloy holds only two FCC solid solutions, FCC_1 (Co,Cr-rich) and FCC_2 (Cu-rich), with no intermetallic. 2 h at 800 C precipitates a Cr-rich sigma phase with tetragonal structure.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (STR/phase/identity), n9 (STR/phase/identity), n11 (STR/microstructure/feature_size). Premises: Earlier work [31] identified the two FCC phases of this alloy: FCC_1 rich in Co and Cr, FCC_2 rich in Cu

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Sigma precipitation is set jointly by the thermodynamic driving force and sluggish solid-state diffusion, so 2 h below 800 C is too short to nucleate it. Finer, denser nanoprecipitates raise the obstacle density against dislocation glide, so strength rises while ductility falls.
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (MEC/pathway), n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (MEC/pathway), n13 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value). Premises: Solid-state diffusion is far slower than the few minutes of solidification and cooling on a water-cooled copper hearth; Finer, more closely spaced precipitates give a higher obstacle density to dislocation glide, raising strength and cutting uniform ductility; Sigma phases in Cr-bearing alloys are hard and brittle, so coarse sigma particles embrittle an FCC matrix

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The alloy keeps a usable strength-ductility balance only for anneals up to 600 C; anneals at 800 and 1000 C disqualify it

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Sigma formation is deleterious to the tensile properties of this HEA

nodes.note: Cr map otherwise near-black, so the matrix is Cr-poor; the Co, Mn and Ni maps (F2d, F2g, F2h) show no visible enrichment at the particles even though the text gives sigma ~27 at.% Co

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, F4, F6
nodes.head: Energy minima relative to FCC-FM: FCC-PM +0.33, HCP-FM +0.78, HCP-PM +1.0, BCC-FM +1.42, BCC-PM +2.35 mRy. EDS table printed on the micrograph: FCC_1 Cr 24.11 / Mn 15.38 / Co 25.07 / Ni 25.95 / Cu 09.50; FCC_2 Cr 02.86 / Mn 25.28 / Co 04.98 / Ni 22.37 / Cu 44.51 at.%.
nodes.op: cross check consistency, read characteristic point
nodes.note: minima at Wigner-Seitz radius ~2.67-2.70 Bohr; FCC-FM is the zero of the plot the packet lists no OCR for this whole-figure crop, so the table was read from the pixels; the two red boxes mark where each spectrum was taken HCP-FM is also within ~0.8 mRy (~11 meV/atom) of FCC-FM, so the calculation orders the structures but does not exclude them at temperature
nodes.detail: o9: Energy minima relative to FCC-FM: FCC-PM +0.33, HCP-FM +0.78, HCP-PM +1.0, BCC-FM +1.42, BCC-PM +2.35 mRy; o10: EDS table printed on the micrograph: FCC_1 Cr 24.11 / Mn 15.38 / Co 25.07 / Ni 25.95 / Cu 09.50; FCC_2 Cr 02.86 / Mn 25.28 / Co 04.98 / Ni 22.37 / Cu 44.51 at.%; a4: The FCC-FM to FCC-PM separation is only ~0.33 mRy (~4.5 meV/atom), far below kT at the annealing temperatures

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: Computed sigma fraction falls from ~0.11 at 200 C to zero at ~870 C; FCC_L12#1 appears only above ~690 C and peaks ~0.17 at ~840 C; FCC_L12#2 stays ~0.83-0.92
nodes.note: liquid enters at ~1010 C and is complete by ~1060 C; the sigma solvus reads ~870 C on the axis, the text says 'approximately 850 C'

nodes.title: evidence, F7
nodes.head: Across the sweep sigma_u and sigma_y rise from Cast to a maximum at 600 C then fall steeply at 800 and 1000 C, while elongation falls monotonically from ~35 % to 0. Engineering curves: 600 C peaks ~825 MPa at ~18 % strain; Cast and 200 C ~695 MPa at ~35 %; 400 C ~680 MPa at ~22.5 %; 800 C ~530 MPa at ~15 %; 1000 C fractures ~110 MPa below 0.5 %
nodes.solves: Yield and ultimate tensile strength rise to a maximum at 600 C (~580 and ~825 MPa) while elongation falls from ~35 to ~22 %
nodes.note: one specimen per condition, no error bars; the sigma_u panel has no zero tick so the 1000 C point sits below the lowest label the 1000 C curve is the arrowed navy trace at the origin; specimen drawing inset gives a 10 mm x 2 mm x 1 mm gauge
